name: agent-avatar

frames.best_why: The large avatar shows its six-by-six pixel pattern most clearly, with the six agent cards all visible.

tagline: Round pixel-grid avatars generated from a name, each a different colour.
summary: Generative avatars drawn on canvas: a circular six-by-six grid of coloured squares derived from a string seed. Each cell slowly pulses, sweeps and occasionally sparkles, so no two agents look alike.
appearance: Perfectly round avatars made of six-by-six blocks in one tight hue, from lime green to magenta and blue. Each has a dark backing and a faint glow; the small ones sit in bordered cards beside names and roles.
behaviour: Cells brighten and dim at different rates, a diagonal wave crosses the grid, and a few cells flash brighter. The whole disc also breathes very slightly in size.
demo_content: Six agents: Atlas, Juniper, Orion, Wren, Sable and Kestrel with roles and status lines.
use_when: Multiple agents or users need distinct avatars without photos, derived reliably from their name.
avoid_when: It is canvas-only and decorative, and tiny sizes lose the six-by-six pattern to blur.
customise: Seed string, pixel size and an animated flag are props; the palette, grid and animation constants are fixed in the source.
weight_why: Each avatar runs its own canvas loop, drawing 36 cells with a blur shadow per frame.

a11y.note: Each canvas is labelled and stops animating under reduced motion; there is nothing to operate.

issues: Small avatars read as fuzzy blobs; the six-by-six grid only resolves at the large size.
polish_why: Distinctive generated avatars with a nice glow; the smallest size blurs the pixel pattern away.
